clue.text: Father requiring pair of pears, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means keep only the letters in odd positions of each pear

parts.note: a pair of pears is two pears, so the fruit's name written twice

explanation.surface: A dad who insists on a couple of pears, for some peculiar reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' keeps the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the doubled fruit name.
explanation.definitionFit: Papa is an old-fashioned, affectionate word a child uses for a male parent.

clue.text: Feast in fruit for large animal

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, here the verb placed within the fruit

parts.note: a grape is a fruit
to feast is to eat

explanation.surface: A big creature gorging itself inside an orchard or fruit bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A great ape, such as a gorilla or orangutan, is a large primate, so a big animal.

clue.text: Sturdy bill prodding fruit, first of oils extracted

indicators.note: something prodding pokes into another thing, so the bill goes inside the fruit
extracted means a letter is pulled out of the fruit

parts.note: a sloe is a small sour fruit of the blackthorn

indicators.note: first of means take only the opening letter of oils

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in running up a tab at a bar

explanation.surface: A sturdy beak pecking at a piece of fruit from which oil has been pressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like a beak but is a tab, as in a bar bill. 'first of oils extracted' removes the O; 'prodding' pushes the bill into what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is firm and steady, the same quality as being sturdy.

clue.text: US president with endless fruit: a good deal to eat, but no starter

indicators.note: to eat means the fruit takes the other piece inside itself
endless means the last letter of the fruit is dropped

parts.note: a banana is a fruit

indicators.note: no starter means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a good deal means much, a large amount

explanation.surface: A president with a never-ending fruit bowl, who eats plenty but skips the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' and 'but no starter' trim the two words at opposite ends; 'to eat' sets the second piece inside the first, after its opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: James Buchanan was the fifteenth President of the United States, serving just before Lincoln.

clue.text: Nothing is fruit

parts.note: nothing is zero, written as the letter O
to be, or exist, is to live: he is, he lives

explanation.surface: A blunt claim that nothing else counts but fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Olives are the small oily stone fruits of the olive tree.

clue.text: Country importing really amazing nectarines, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the opening letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A nation that brings in wonderful nectarines from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'importing' looks like a containment signal, but here it simply supplies its own first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia, formerly known as Persia.

clue.text: Orange books in lift

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other, the books going into the lift

parts.note: to lift something is to carry it
OT is the Old Testament, the first books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Orange-covered volumes going up in an elevator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' reads as an elevator but is the verb, meaning carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Carroty describes a ginger hue like that of a carrot, an orange colour.

clue.text: Everything flipping right in lemon fool

indicators.note: in signals that these pieces go inside the lemon

parts.note: a lemon is a dud, a thing that fails to work

indicators.note: flipping turns the word for everything over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: everything means all

explanation.surface: A cook stirring everything into a lemon fool, a creamy fruit dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns ALL into LLA; with R it goes 'in' DUD. 'lemon fool' looks like the pudding, but lemon is the dud and fool the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dullard is a slow, stupid person, which is what calling someone a fool means.

clue.text: Hybrid melon, one scooped out for party

indicators.note: scooped out suggests hollowing a melon, here removing a letter

parts.note: the Galia is a hybrid variety of melon
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A melon with one portion spooned out, ready to serve at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A gala is a festive occasion or celebration, a kind of party.

clue.text: Maestro placing last bits of crab apple on the new cooker

indicators.note: last bits means the final letter of each of these two words
new means the letters of the word are made fresh, rearranged

parts.note: an oven is a cooker

explanation.surface: A chef putting the ends of crab apples on a brand-new stove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals that the word 'the' is rearranged, giving ETH.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven, the German composer, is a great master of music, the meaning of maestro.

clue.text: Passing hard prune stone, with Pepe's bowels opening?

indicators.note: opening means this piece comes at the start of the answer
the bowels are the insides, so the inner letters of the name

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

indicators.note: to prune is to cut back, here trimming the final letter

parts.note: an emerald is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A lavatorial picture of someone passing a hard prune stone with loosened bowels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prune' looks like the dried plum but is the verb, trimming the gem's last letter. 'bowels' takes the inner letters of Pepe, and 'opening' puts them first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral describes something short-lived, fleeting or passing quickly.

clue.text: Extra strawberries finally cut

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter of strawberries

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim

explanation.surface: Some additional strawberries, sliced up at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare means additional, kept beyond what is needed, so extra.

clue.text: Date boxes in European river

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to date someone is to see them romantically

explanation.surface: A date fruit packed in boxes, shipped along a European river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Date' suggests the fruit or a calendar day but is the verb, as in seeing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seine is the river that runs through Paris, in France.

clue.text: Large ripe damson that man has picked

indicators.note: has picked means holding, so one piece is gathered up inside the other

parts.note: that man is he

indicators.note: ripe fruit is soft and changed, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A man has picked a big, ripe damson plum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripe' signals the anagram of damson; 'has picked' means the pronoun holds the result. 'Large' is the definition, as in a large sum.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome sum or profit is a large, generous one.

clue.text: David's subject picking up some fruit, a rambutan

indicators.note: in a down answer, picking up means reading upwards, so backwards
some means just part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A painter choosing a still life of fruit, a rambutan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes TARAM from fruiT A RAMbutan and 'picking up' reverses it. David is the painter Jacques-Louis David.
explanation.definitionFit: David painted The Death of Marat, showing the French revolutionary murdered in his bath.

clue.text: Fruit in slippery gunk, initially wiped

indicators.note: initially wiped means the opening letter is cleaned away

parts.note: slime is slippery gunk

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit lying in slimy muck, given a quick wipe first.
explanation.definitionFit: A lime is a small green citrus fruit.

clue.text: Japanese food: a little clementine marked 'From the East'

indicators.note: in an across answer, from the east means reading right to left, so backwards
a little means only part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A clementine stamped with a label saying it was imported from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' takes NEMAR from clementiNE MARked; 'From the East' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramen is a Japanese dish of wheat noodles in broth.

clue.text: Staff pressing fruit for Bacchus, say?

indicators.note: pressing means squeezing something, so it is held inside the staff

parts.note: a staff is a rod
a mango is a fruit

explanation.surface: Using a pole to press fruit into wine for the god of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchus is the Roman deity of wine, an example of a Roman god, hence 'say?'.

clue.text: Renaissance composer producing sound of kiwi, say?

indicators.note: sound of tells us the answer is how a word is said, not spelt

parts.note: a kiwi is a flightless New Zealand bird, so an example of one

explanation.surface: A composer writing music that imitates the cry of a kiwi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kiwi' suggests the fruit, in keeping with the puzzle, but it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: William Byrd was an English composer of the late sixteenth century, the Renaissance period.

clue.text: Event finding seed in pear, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear tells us the fruit stands for a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a pear stands for the same-sounding pair, in rowing a boat for two oarsmen
seed means offspring or lineage, as in a race of people

explanation.surface: Something found by cutting into a pear, so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pear' is heard as 'pair', a two-oared rowing boat; 'seed' means descendants, a race. The Boat Race is the yearly Oxford v Cambridge rowing contest on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boat Race is an annual sporting event between the rowing crews of Oxford and Cambridge.

clue.text: Cherry always cut by me for saviour

parts.note: cherry is a shade of red

indicators.note: cut by means the second word interrupts the first, going inside it

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Someone claiming to rescue a cherry tree by pruning it themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'always' gives the poetic contraction of ever; 'cut by' puts the word me inside it, just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A redeemer is one who rescues or delivers others; in Christianity it is a title of Christ.

clue.text: Involve last of fruit in a line, stewed

indicators.note: in means this letter goes into the jumbled letters
stewed fruit is cooked down and mixed, so the letters are scrambled
last of takes the final letter of the word fruit

explanation.surface: A recipe step: put the end of the fruit into a row and stew it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stewed' rearranges A and LINE together; 'in' places the T from fruit inside the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve or require something as a necessary part.

clue.text: Yet to consume each peach

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: yet means but, as in small yet strong

explanation.surface: Still waiting to eat a peach, one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peach' looks like the fruit, but it is the informal noun for a fine thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaut and a peach are both informal words for something or someone excellent.

clue.text: Spiritual teacher with friend had nuts

parts.note: bud is informal for a friend

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and rearrange

explanation.surface: A guru whose companion had been snacking on nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' rearranges HAD into DHA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Buddha, Siddhartha Gautama, founded Buddhism and taught enlightenment.

clue.text: Confused flavour, lychee lacking pulp in conclusion

indicators.note: in shows these pieces placed within the conclusion

parts.note: a conclusion is an end
tang is a sharp flavour

indicators.note: lacking pulp means the soft inner flesh is removed, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Puzzled by the taste of a lychee with its flesh gone at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking pulp' keeps only the outer letters of lychee; 'in conclusion' puts the flavour plus those letters inside a word for conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entangled means caught up and muddled, so mixed up or confused.

clue.text: See inexpensive fruits, cheap and nasty, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: Look at these bargain fruits, which are low-priced and low-quality in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of or spot, an old literary word for seeing.

clue.text: Some of the durian rejected — like a raspberry?

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters are read backwards
some of means only part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bite of notoriously smelly durian sent back, rather like a sour raspberry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of' takes EDUR from thE DURian; 'rejected' turns it around. 'raspberry' is not the fruit but the rude noise blown with the tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing a raspberry makes a vulgar noise of contempt, so it is impolite.

clue.text: Dodge mandarin, for example

definitions.meaning: to dodge, bending out of the way
the mandarin is a colourful species of ...

explanation.definitionFit: Duck means both to evade by bending down and a waterbird, of which the mandarin is one kind.

clue.text: A jar containing mostly mellow fruit

indicators.note: containing means the jar holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a jar is a pot

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: mellow means rich, as in a full, smooth flavour

explanation.surface: A jar holding fruit that is almost fully ripened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of rich; 'containing' puts what remains inside the jar.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a soft orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Sweet plum filled with cream, originally

indicators.note: filled with means the first word has the next piece stuffed inside it

parts.note: a plum job is a choice one, the best pick

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter of cream

explanation.surface: A dessert of plums stuffed with cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plum' looks like the fruit but is the adjective meaning choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A choc ice is a block of ice cream coated in chocolate, a frozen sweet treat.
